controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.4 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.4 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="CreatePolicy" OR eventName="AttachUserPolicy" OR eventName="AttachRolePolicy" OR eventName="PutUserPolicy" OR eventName="PutRolePolicy" OR eventName="CreateRole")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.4_iam_policy_changes_4"
| sort -_time
description: IAM policy changes affect who can do what across the entire AWS account. Unauthorized policy attachments can grant admin access.
value: Detecting iam policy changes early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Alert on all IAM policy modifications. Critical alert when AdministratorAccess or PowerUserAccess policies are attached. Track with change management.
visualization: Table, Timeline, Bar chart by event type.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  where All_Changes.object_category="policy" OR match(All_Changes.object, "(?i)IAMPolicy|iam:policy")
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Alert on all IAM policy modifications. Critical alert when AdministratorAccess or PowerUserAccess policies are attached. Track with change management.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (eventName="CreatePolicy" OR eventName="AttachUserPolicy" OR eventName="AttachRolePolicy" OR eventName="PutUserPolicy" OR eventName="PutRolePolicy" OR eventName="CreateRole")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.4_iam_policy_changes_4"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect iam policy changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_4_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table, Timeline, Bar chart by event type..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of iam policy changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
